title: Generosity part 4
devotional:
2 Corinthians 8:1-9

‘’And now, brothers and sisters, we want you to know about the grace that God has given the Macedonian churches. In the midst of a very severe trial, their overflowing joy and their extreme poverty welled up in rich generosity. For I testify that they gave as much as they were able, and even beyond their ability. Entirely on their own, they urgently pleaded with us for the privilege of sharing in this service to the Lord’s people. And they exceeded our expectations: They gave themselves first of all to the Lord, and then by the will of God also to us. So we urged Titus, just as he had earlier made a beginning, to bring also to completion this act of grace on your part. But since you excel in everything—in faith, in speech, in knowledge, in complete earnestness and in the love we have kindled in you—see that you also excel in this grace of giving. I am not commanding you, but I want to test the sincerity of your love by comparing it with the earnestness of others. For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sake he became poor, so that you through his poverty might become rich.’’

Paul had a lot to say about the heart behind their giving.

1.They gave because they had experienced the grace of God. ‘And now brothers we want you to know about the grace God has given the Macedonian churches.’

The grace of God in someone’s life will always have a radical effect. Generosity is the result of God’s grace transforming a person’s heart. When we allow the grace of God to transform our hearts our whole perspective about ourselves and our world view are completely changed. We discover a truth that we had never known before.

We discover that we are completely loved. No matter what we do, or don’t do God will always love us. As we truly realise this truth, we will experience a deep feeling of security.

We will discover that the things we possess and the things we achieve can never add value to us as people. This is really important, because wrongly, we hold on tight to things and positions because we believe that these things are an integral part of our value as people.

We discover that all people are worth loving, because we are all made in the image of God.

2.They gave despite their own pain. ‘Out of the most severe trial.’ The word “affliction” ‘severe trial’ (THLIPSIS) in the Greek literally refers to pressure as in crushing grapes. Figuratively, in light of this context it would describe the extreme pressure the Macedonians were under, while engaging in their generous giving. Paul does not say what the trial is that he is referring to but we do know from other scriptures that the churches in Macedonia were persecuted.

“For you, brethren, became imitators of the churches of God in Christ Jesus that are in Judea, for you also endured the same sufferings at the hands of your own countrymen, even as they did from the Jews, who both killed the Lord Jesus and the prophets, and drove us out.” (1 Thessalonians 2:14-15.)

So, what was the nature of the ordeal that was afflicting the churches of Macedonia? The Macedonian believers were being persecuted by their own countrymen in a similar manner as their Jewish brethren in Judea had been persecuted by their countrymen.

These believers were in the most severe trial despite being filled with the grace of God. The grace of God is not a panacea for all our problems. It will not take away all our trouble, but it will help us to respond to others in a healthy manner without becoming bitter, angry or selfish.

3.They gave out of overflowing joy.

They gave out of hearts that were filled with joy. Joy is more than an emotion, it is proof of spiritual growth and maturity. It is not the consequence of circumstances; rather it is the result of the fruit of the Spirit growing in someone’s life. See Galatians 5:22. The best way to understand this kind of Joy is to realise that the opposite of this Joy is not sadness but hopelessness. I think it would be difficult to be mean spirited and have joy in your heart at the same time. Joy breaks down the walls that separate people, it empowers people to see beyond themselves and take the needs of others seriously.

It is interesting to note that Jesus spoke most about his own joy on the night before his cruel death on the cross than at any other time. The word Paul uses for joy comes from the word that means grace.
prayer: Father help me understand that generosity has nothing to do with circumstances or bank balance.
